title: November Patch Tuesday: How to Sort Through the Patches
content_md: Key Takeaways At 1,252 CVEs this month, “patch everything now” isn’t a plan; teams need to decide what to patch first, what to test, and what to mitigate. Know your exposure early: Qualys InstaScan flagged affected assets about 40 minutes before Microsoft’s release notes page finished loading, with no new scan. Not every patch is safe on day one: about 35% of November patches earned a Low reliability rating from Qualys, based on public signals and telemetry from 500M+ deployed patches. Deploy in waves: proven risky exposures first, low-impact patches on automation, and high-impact patches through pilot rings. When a critical patch breaks, mitigate with a compensating control, then patch and retire the mitigation once a fixed update ships. Every Patch Tuesday forces the same trade-off. Patch too slowly, and attackers get a head start on newly disclosed vulnerabilities. Patch too quickly, and a bad update can take down Exchange, break line-of-business apps, or trigger a wave of help desk tickets. November 2026 showed both sides of that tension. Our data pointed to three lessons security and IT teams can use this month and every month: Know your exposure before the details are public Check whether a patch is reliable before you push it Have a fallback when it isn’t November at a glance In November 2025, Microsoft addressed 63 CVEs on Patch Tuesday. In November 2026 , with frontier AI models now accelerating vulnerability discovery, that number reached 1,252, nearly 20 times high
